audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf's W is described as omnivamp that 'out-heals his clone-poke trades' and 'out-sustains him'. Riot's text for Olaf's W is attack speed plus a shield; the life steal is on the passive, Berserker Rage, and scales with missing health.
audit.why: It changes the all-in maths a player runs at level 6: a shield is a one-off buffer against Cyclone's burst, not a sustain race he can win by standing in it.
audit.corrected: W shields and gives attack speed; the passive life steal ramps as you drop low.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gives Olaf Level 1 as 'Skill' and hands him both item rows, while whys[0] says Olaf wins first contact clean, whys[5] calls first item a coinflip and whys[6] says Wukong out-scales at two items.
audit.why: Three rows disagree with the prose immediately beside them and with the packet chart, on a 49.93% lane that should read as even overall with an early tilt.
audit.corrected: Olaf Levels 1-3; Skill at 4-5, 6 and first item; Wukong at two-plus items.

audit.why: Spike shape is right — Olaf at 2-3 before Crushing Blow's shred and Warrior Trickster are online, Wukong at two-plus items. No cooldown numbers could be added on Wukong's side because the brief supplies no kit for him (enemyKit is null), and inventing them would be worse than omitting them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf's kit file carries a derived flag on Undertow reading 'grounding — shuts off enemy dashes'.
audit.why: Riot's own description of Undertow is an axe that damages, reduces Armor and slows — no grounding. Per the standing rule, the description wins. Advice built on Undertow denying Nimbus Strike would be false.
audit.corrected: Undertow slows and shreds armour; it does not deny his dash. Make him spend Nimbus Strike, then stick with axe resets.

audit.why: 49.93% over 1494 games — a true coinflip, matching 'EVEN'.

edits.before: Black Cleaver plus Bramble at your lane-bully peak — chunk him with E and let W omnivamp out-heal his clone-poke trades.
edits.after: Black Cleaver plus Bramble at your lane-bully peak — chunk him with Reckless Swing and let W's shield eat his answer.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 even out as his W clone comes online and his Q shreds your armor, so respect the juke. The clone mimics his animations, so do not blow E or Q on the decoy, wait the half-second to confirm the real Wukong before you commit your true-damage nuke. At 6 your Ragnarok is the answer to his all-in: pop it as he casts R and the spin knockup does nothing, leaving you free to E and let W omnivamp out-sustain him while his clone burst fizzles.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 even out as Warrior Trickster comes online and Crushing Blow shreds your armor, so respect the juke. The clone mimics his animations — do not spend Undertow or Reckless Swing on the decoy, wait the half-second to confirm the real Wukong. At 6 Ragnarok is the answer to his all-in: press it as he casts Cyclone and the knockup does nothing, leaving you free to swing while your passive life steal ramps and his burst fizzles.

edits.before: This is where Wukong takes over. His stacked armor blunts your autos and W omnivamp, his Q shred and clone let him burst you in a teamfight, and his R knockup catches you the moment Ragnarok is down. Your flat E true damage and short-fight kit lose value while he scales item-dependent. Build Bramble and push your early-to-mid lead into towers and objectives, because if the game goes long his clone-and-knockup combo wins the fights yours can no longer reach.
edits.after: This is where Wukong takes over. Stacked armor blunts your autos, Crushing Blow's shred and the clone let him burst you in a teamfight, and Cyclone catches you the moment Ragnarok's 100 seconds are down. Your flat true damage and short-fight kit lose value while he scales item-dependent. Build Bramble and push your early-to-mid lead into towers and objectives, because if the game goes long his clone-and-knockup combo wins the fights yours can no longer reach.

edits.after: Ragnarok answers his Cyclone knockup — it is 100s at rank 1, so spend it only on a kill

notes: The brief carries enemyKit: null for Wukong, so no Wukong cooldowns, ranges or flags were available and none were invented — every number added here is Olaf's own.
